hints: Consider how the amplifier gain behaves across different input signal frequencies.
State that the gain remains the same (constant) for all frequencies.
walkthrough: Bandwidth refers to the range of signal frequencies over which an amplifier operates with full gain.
Infinite bandwidth means that the amplifier provides the same voltage gain for all signal frequencies without attenuation or frequency cut-off.

ai_rubric.observable: States gain is the same for all frequencies (or constant gain across all frequencies).

hints: Consider how quickly the output voltage responds when a sudden change occurs at the input.
State that changes in output voltage happen instantaneously, with no time delay when input changes.
walkthrough: Slew rate describes the maximum rate of change of output voltage per unit time.
Infinite slew rate means that the output voltage responds instantaneously with zero time delay when the input voltage changes.

ai_rubric.observable: States no (time) delay in change in output when input is changed (or instantaneous output response).

hints: Identify the saturation output voltage from the op-amp supply rails shown in Fig. 8.1.
Calculate the voltage gain using $\text{gain} = \frac{V_{\mathrm{OUT}}}{V_{\mathrm{IN}}}$ with saturation voltage $V_{\mathrm{OUT}} = 5.0\,\mathrm{V}$ and input $V_{\mathrm{IN}} = 0.40\,\mathrm{V}$.
walkthrough: From the supply rails $+5.0\,\mathrm{V}$ and $-5.0\,\mathrm{V}$ in Fig. 8.1, the output voltage at the point of saturation is $V_{\mathrm{OUT}} = 5.0\,\mathrm{V}$.
The voltage gain of the amplifier is $\text{gain} = \frac{V_{\mathrm{OUT}}}{V_{\mathrm{IN}}} = \frac{5.0}{0.40} = 12.5$ (or 13).

hints: Recall the gain equation for a non-inverting operational amplifier circuit in terms of feedback resistor R and resistor $R_1 = 800\,\Omega$.
walkthrough: The amplifier in Fig. 8.1 is connected in non-inverting mode, so its voltage gain is given by $G = 1 + \frac{R}{R_1} = 1 + \frac{R}{800}$.
